issues.description: Field 'numberOfTutors' in the Lecture class is declared with different types across artifacts. The UML in problem_statement.md specifies numberOfTutors as type int (Lecture UML: lines show '-numberOfTutors: int'), while the reference implementation in solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java declares the field as 'private short numberOfTutors;' (field declaration at line 10) and uses 'short' in the constructor parameter (constructor signature at line 13) and the setter signature (setNumberOfTutors(short) at line 58). This inconsistency between the specification and the reference implementation can confuse students about the intended type and may lead to mismatches with tests or with code they write expecting an int.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of numberOfTutors consistent across all artifacts. Either change the solution implementation to use 'int' for the field, constructor parameter, and setter (preferred to match the UML), or update the problem statement/UML to declare numberOfTutors as 'short' and adjust the textual description accordingly. Ensure tests and any examples use the same type.
